svg.title: A charge nurse takes report on four clients. Client A: 68, day 1 after bowel resection, incision pain 6 of 10. Client B: 54, on a heparin infusion for a clot, now with new confusion and left-sided weakness. Client C: 80, stable and waiting for discharge teaching. Client D: 45, due for a routine dressing change.
svg.desc: New confusion with one-sided weakness in a client receiving heparin is a possible intracranial bleed, the only problem on this list that can kill within the hour. Pain of 6 of 10 is genuine and gets treated, just not ahead of a possible bleed, which makes it the tempting condition to choose. Discharge teaching cannot be delegated to assistive personnel, because teaching requires nursing judgment and stays with the licensed nurse.
